newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends slightly lower, gilt prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends slightly lower, gilt prices mixed.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed slightly lower at 7.00-7.50 percent on Tuesday compared to the day's opening levels of 8.50-9.50 percent, dealers said.
The call rates saw a high of 9.50 percent and a low of 6.50 percent, dealers said.
"Rates may open in the region of 8.50-9.00 percent on Wednesday," a dealer said.
Indian government said on Tuesday that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will auction 20 billion rupees worth of seven-year dated securities on June 17.
The new auction clubed with the advance tax payment estimated at 20 billion rupees and the outflow on account of food-credit will push the call rates northwards, dealers said.

The securities market saw a mixed response -- prices fell in the opening session on selling pressure but firmed up on buying interest in mid-session and fell again in the closing session on the announcement on new seven-year bond auction, dealers said.

The 12.69 percent government stock 2002 saw deals ranging from 100.85 rupees to 101.08 ruppes but fell towards the close to 101.00 rupees, lower compared to its previous close of 101.15 rupees, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in April saw trades at 8.90 percent and 8.95 percent compared to the previous 8.95 percent.
The 60 days maturity certificate of deposits was quoted at 7.00-7.50 percent and the P1+ rated commercial paper maturing in August was quoted at 9.00-9.50 percent in the secondary market.
